newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Xinjiang 1997 lithium exports to plunge.
newsitem.headline: China's Xinjiang 1997 lithium exports to plunge.

text.p: China's exports of lithium carbonate from the western Xinjiang Autonomous Region will drop sharply this year after a dip in world prices, a government metals official from the region said on Tuesday.

"Our exports of lithium carbonate and lithium hydroxide this year will drop to about 1,000 tonnes, compared to 3,000 tonnes in 1996," an official from the China National Import Export Corporation in Xinjiang told Reuters.
"The main reason is production costs (internationally) have dropped and the price has dropped after Chile started producing lithium with brine," he said.
The official was participating in a China non-ferrous metals fair being held in Hong Kong this week.
"This year our offer price for lithium carbonate has dropped to about $2,500 per tonne, compared to our offer price of about $3,300 per tonne in 1996," the official said.
Sociedad Quimica y Minera de Chile SA's lithium production at its Minsal salt lake mine in northern Chile had brought the cost of production down globally, he said.
"China's lithium is produced from spodumene, and compared to brine, it's very expensive," the official said.
